name: com.menfem/mcp
title: MenFem
description: AI infrastructure and markets, with our own money in: calls, company research, compute data.

tools.name: findArticles
tools.description: Search MenFem's published articles by title and excerpt. Returns up to 20 matches with slug, title, excerpt, and publish date.

tools.name: checkClaim
tools.description: Search The Primary Record — MenFem's ledger of market-moving claims graded against companies' own primary documents. Returns each claim's sourcing grade (anonymous/named/official-filing), what the company's attested filing says, and whether it was CONFIRMED, DENIED, PARTIAL, or is still OPEN. Use to answer 'was that report ever confirmed?' or 'what does the filing actually say?'.

query.description: Company name, ticker, or claim keywords.

status.description: Optional filter: OPEN, CONFIRMED, DENIED, or PARTIAL.

tools.name: findCompanies
tools.description: Search MenFem's company database by name and description. Uses full-text search with trigram fallback. Results can be companies or glossary entries; each carries `kind` saying which, and an absolute `url` to cite. A company result carries `tracked` (on the startups roster) and `reviewState` (`none` · `first-look` · `scored`, from its newest public review; null when it could not be read). A first look carries no score and must never be quoted with one: getCompanyDossier has the review. Pass `beat` (a company beat) for every published company on that beat, by name and paged with `offset`; a beat MenFem has no companies on answers with the beats it does.

query.description: Words to search for. Optional with `beat`, where it filters by name.

beat.description: A company beat: lists that beat's published companies, by name.

offset.description: With `beat`: how many companies to skip; pass the nextOffset of the page before.

tools.name: getRecentMarketCalls
tools.description: List MenFem's most recently published market calls — on-the-record predictions with entry prices and time horizons. A row is a summary by default, without the thesis; pass detail: "full" for the thesis. It pages: total is every open call, and nextOffset, when it is not null, is the offset of the next page.

offset.description: How many calls to skip, newest first: pass the nextOffset of the page before.

detail.description: summary (default) leaves out each thesis; full returns it.

tools.name: getTokenPrices
tools.description: Per-model LLM inference list prices — a DATED, HAND-READ price table, not a live index. The swept Token Price Index was retired on 2026-08-19; what this returns is the constant that replaced it, stamped with the date it was read (see the `observedAt` on the response and on every row). Treat a row as a historical observation, not a current quote, and re-check the provider before quoting a price. Returns one row per model (input/output $ per Mtok, cached-input price, context window), filterable by capability tier, access (open-weight vs closed-API), and provider. Fully open — no auth or scope required. Earlier readings are no longer published: the archive that held them went with /datasets on 2026-09-12.

access.description: Filter by model access — open-weight or closed/API-only.

provider.description: Filter by provider name (case-insensitive substring match).

tools.name: getPriceSpreads
tools.description: Open-vs-closed price spreads — per capability tier, the cheapest open-weight vs closed-API model price and the resulting cost multiple, computed across three workload profiles (general/agentic/reasoning, weighted by input:output ratio). Derived from the same DATED, HAND-READ price table as getTokenPrices: the swept Token Price Index was retired on 2026-08-19, so the response `observedAt` is when the underlying prices were read, not now. Fully open — no auth or scope required.

tier.description: Optional capability-tier filter (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "frontier"). Omit for all tiers.

tools.name: getPosition
tools.description: What MenFem currently holds on a company, a ticker or a beat, assembled from the published record with no model and no generated prose: its open market calls (with the falsifier) and the latest resolved ones with their grades, the Primary Record claims about it with their status, and the newest pieces with their verdict and tell. Every item carries its canonical url and its markdown twin (mdUrl). The subject resolves, in order, to a published company by slug, ticker or name (or its Subject record), a company beat such as 'datacenters', or a ticker that calls or claims carry. When nothing matches, `found` is false and `suggestions` names companies whose name contains the text. A market call or a verdict is a stated view, not investment advice.

subject.description: A company slug, name or ticker ('nvidia', 'NVDA'), or a beat ('datacenters').

tools.name: getWhatsNew
tools.description: What MenFem published, and which of its calls' tells moved, since a moment you give. Each piece carries its Bet Lens verdict (good, live, lucky or bad), the tell — the thing that would settle the call — and the tell's status (open, moved or settled), plus the MenFem Principles it is played by. tellsMoved lists pieces whose tell moved or settled in the window: watch a tell to know when MenFem's call moves. calls lists market calls opened, reviewed or resolved in the window, each with its falsifier exactly as published or null. Pass the returned `now` back as `since` next time. A verdict is a stated view on a decision, never advice. Fully open — no key required.

since.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime; returns what happened after it. Default: 7 days ago.

beats.description: Only these beats — category slugs (e.g. "datacenters") or lanes (e.g. "markets"). Default: all.

tools.name: getBeatIndex
tools.description: One beat's index: the full stored weekly curve, this week's move, and the top/bottom constituent movers behind it. Returns found:false for a beat that has never met the minimum-constituent bar — that beat has no curve yet, not an empty one.

tools.name: getCompanyEvents
tools.description: What has happened to one published company — the typed event rows the sweep deposits (guidance, deployments, site news, contracts, filings, regulatory moves, price moves, export controls, clearances) plus dossier-change rows, newest first. Takes a slug, or a ticker or exact company name, which it resolves to the slug (company.slug says which). Returns found:false when nothing published matches, with suggestions when several do.

slug.description: Company slug, e.g. "nebius", or its ticker or exact name, e.g. "NBIS".

tools.name: getPrintBaseRate
tools.description: One ticker's print base rate: how many of its earnings prints have been graded, how many closed up, the median absolute move, and the most recent graded prints. A ticker with nothing graded gets an honest empty record (graded: 0), never null.

tools.name: getSeries
tools.description: A named collector series from MenFem's data register — a dated, cron-written record, never a live fetch. Pass `key` for one sub-series (a ticker, a reactor unit, a model id, a material), oldest first; omit it for the newest point per key across the whole series. An unknown seriesId is answered with the list of known series.

key.description: Optional sub-series key. Omit for the latest snapshot across all keys.

limit.description: Max points when `key` is given (1-500, default 400).

tools.name: getHardwarePrices
tools.description: The latest cron-written price for every (SKU, provider, term, region) of one hardware-price kind — GPU rental $/GPU-hour, GPU used-market, DRAM spot, HBM contract, NAND spot. Each row says its `term` (SPOT, ON_DEMAND, RESERVED_1Y/3Y/5Y …) and its `basis`: OBSERVED_OFFER is what a marketplace host is asking (Vast), LIST is a provider's own published rate card (Azure, region eastus). The two are different claims — never blend or average a list price with an observed offer. Pass `term` and/or `basis` to narrow. Every row is fetched keyless from a public endpoint; a SKU nobody priced this week keeps its last real week (visible via `weekEnding`) rather than disappearing.

term.description: Optional. Only rows on this commitment term, e.g. "RESERVED_1Y".

basis.description: Optional. OBSERVED_OFFER (marketplace asks) or LIST (rate cards).

tools.name: getComputeDeals
tools.description: MenFem's compute Ledger: the published deals behind the compute market — capacity contracts, loans against GPUs, backstops, equity stakes, site leases, chip supply, power deals and acquisitions — newest announcement first. Each row carries the day it was announced, its parties and their roles, the headline value as disclosed (US$ millions; null when undisclosed), term, rate and size where stated, and the source URL with its kind. A REPORTED row is a news report and is never upgraded to fact without a filing. maturesAt is start plus term, derived here, not reported. Drafts are never returned. A row is a summary by default, without its notes; pass detail: "full" for them.

companySlug.description: Only deals where this MenFem company (its /companies slug, e.g. 'coreweave') is a party.

since.description: Only deals announced on or after this day, YYYY-MM-DD.

detail.description: summary (default) leaves out notes, valueNote, priceNote, sourceLabel and each party's roleLabel; full returns them.

tools.name: getComputeWeek
tools.description: One week (Saturday to Friday) of MenFem's compute board: the Vast.ai H100 SXM observed median for the week and its change on the week before (observed offers both ends), Azure’s H100 list-price ladder for the week with the first week of an unchanged run (list prices only — the two are never combined into one number), the Ledger deals announced that week (dealsAnnounced — a deal belongs to the week it was announced, whenever the Ledger logged it), the rows the Ledger caught up on that week but announced earlier (dealsAddedLate — a backfill, never counted as the week's market), and Connor's take once he has published it. inProgress is true for the week that has not closed — its numbers are so far. weeks lists every week on the board, newest first. report is The Compute Week, MenFem’s weekly report for that week (title, url, excerpt), or null when none is published for it. The same week is on menfem.com/compute.

week.description: The Friday the week ends on, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the week in progress.

tools.name: getComputeCount
tools.description: The Friday Count from MenFem's capacity claims register: how much AI data-centre power was stated as switched on or delivered in a week, from dated statements in company filings and releases and from ERCOT, Texas first. Published statements only. Families are separate readings, each with its own date and source URL — what was filed (switchedOn = ENERGIZED statements, delivered = DELIVERED statements, lateFinds listed apart), the next promise still due, promises falling due and slipping, Epoch AI's estimate (basis EPOCH_ESTIMATE, a covered total, never a world total), ERCOT's meter and gas-queue readings, and EIA-860M gas generation slippage. They are never added together, and megawatts are never summed across bases: every figure carries its basis (critical-it, it-load, gross, contracted-power, nameplate, up-to, unstated, observed-peak; see bases) and every item its source URL and kind. An announcement never counts as capacity. A zero is a counted zero. The footer is part of the answer: "No survey exists. This is a count of statements with sources, not of silicon." Built by the same function as the week's issue (getWeeklyIssue).

week.description: The Friday the week ends on, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the latest closed Friday.

tools.name: getComputeCampuses
tools.description: MenFem's capacity register: the campuses in the register (Texas first) with their published statements, state and promise outcomes, as of today. Each campus carries its stages (the furthest the source statements reach, with megawatts per basis — never one figure across bases), every dated statement with its verbatim quote, basis, source URL and source kind, and its promises read to an outcome (DUE, KEPT, PARTIAL, SLIPPED, NO_STATEMENT, WITHDRAWN or UNREAD — "Not read" is never "no statement found"), with the dates, the grace and the statements that settled each. Epoch AI's per-site estimate sits beside a campus as its own figure (basis EPOCH_ESTIMATE) and never settles a promise. campuses are those with a statement; quiet are registry campuses with none yet. company holds a company's own totals and region ERCOT's readings, both kept apart from the campuses. An announcement never counts as capacity; a campus with no statement in 120 days is marked unverified, not hidden. Published statements only. Filter by campusSlug (one campus; company and region are then left out) and/or party (campuses with a statement by that company, with its company and ERCOT lines; the filter picks campuses and never trims a campus's own statements). The answer is a summary by default, without the verbatim statements; pass campusSlug for one campus in full, or detail: "full".

campusSlug.description: Only this campus, by its register slug (e.g. 'helios'). One of: stargate-abilene, crusoe-abilene-expansion, coreweave-denton, meta-temple, helios, google-midlothian, google-red-oak, microsoft-sat40, microsoft-sat14, vantage-tx1, goodnight, stargate-shackelford, stargate-milam, barber-lake, abernathy, iren-childress, beacon-point, colchis, muskie.

party.description: Only statements made by this party: a company slug as the claims carry it (e.g. 'galaxy-digital', 'coreweave'), or 'ercot'.

detail.description: summary (default) leaves out each campus's statements and their quotes, its sources, aliases, deal slugs and grid, and trims promises and company and region rows to the figure, its basis, the outcome and the source; full returns them all. A campusSlug answer is always full.

tools.name: getWeeklyIssue
tools.description: One issue of The Compute Week, MenFem's weekly report on menfem.com/compute: the four signals (a number, its unit and change, the week its reading is from — a quiet signal shows its last reading, dated — and the trace behind it), the deals announced that week by kind (disclosed values and megawatts summed per kind, never across kinds; added lists what the Ledger caught up on, announced earlier, never counted in the week), the dated catalysts in the week after, and which of the readings behind the stations on /compute moved. take, watching and each signal's read are MenFem's own words and appear only once published; null means none was published. inProgress is true for the week that has not closed. weeks lists every issue, newest first. For the Friday Count use getComputeCount. The answer is a summary by default, without the twelve weeks of deals behind the trend; pass detail: "full" for them. The same week is on menfem.com/compute.

week.description: The Friday the issue ends on, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the latest issue.

detail.description: summary (default) leaves out deals.trend.deals, the twelve weeks of deals getComputeDeals also serves, and counts them in deals.trend.dealCount; full returns them.

tools.name: getComputeQuestions
tools.description: The eight readings behind the stations on menfem.com/compute, each answered as of the latest Friday: the question, today's answer as one number with its sub-line and its trend against four Fridays earlier (up, down, flat, or new), the gauges behind it where a question has several (each says whether the Ledger records it yet — "not recorded yet" is a gap, not a zero), and what would change the answer. A question with no data says "unmeasured" and the first reading it waits for; it is never answered with a proxy. List prices and observed offers are never blended. The would-change line is the falsifier a view on that question hangs off. The same week is on menfem.com/compute, where each answer is a station's reading.

inputSchema.description: No arguments: every question, answered as of the latest Friday.

tools.name: submitConsultingInquiry
tools.description: File a consulting inquiry with MenFem for the person you act for: their business, the one number they want moved and who owns it. Connected to a MenFem account, it is filed under the account's own email and reaches Connor now. Without an account, give the person's email: MenFem emails them a link, and the inquiry reaches Connor only after they click it (inquiry: HELD). It books nothing: the answer carries the booking link and its rule (any weekday from 14:00 UK), and preferredTimes rides the inquiry for Connor to confirm.

door.description: An owner-led business, or a startup.

email.description: The person's email. Required without a MenFem account; ignored for a connected account, whose own email is used.

numberToMove.description: The one number they want moved, in their words (at least 2 characters).

numberOwner.description: Who owns that number (at least 2 characters).

industry.description: Optional. The trade, in their words.

tried.description: Optional. What they have tried so far.

when.description: Optional. When they want to start.

scorecardCode.description: Optional. The code the Scorecard returned, when you ran it for them.

preferredTimes.description: Optional. When they could take a call (weekdays from 14:00 UK). Connor confirms every call himself.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional, for a connected account. Your key for a retry, 1-128 printable characters: a second call with the same key gets the first answer back.

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Tell MenFem what is wrong, missing or worth building: a broken page, a tool you needed and did not find, a question the site could not answer. It lands in the queue Connor triages, marked as sent by an agent. Nothing is sent back.

description.description: What happened, or what is missing, and why it matters.

pageUrl.description: Optional. The menfem.com page it is about.

tools.name: getConsultingOffer
tools.description: MenFem's consulting offer as data, for an agent researching it for a business owner: who it is for, the five-rung cash road with prices (an unset price says "Opening soon"), the Operating Review, the seat with the live number of seats open, the equity road for startups and its disclosure line, the terms, what MenFem will not do, published case studies, how to book an intro call (Connor confirms every call), and how to ask on the person's behalf with `submitConsultingInquiry`. Live counts left out when they cannot be read, never guessed. The same text as markdown: the resource menfem://consulting or https://menfem.com/consulting.md.

tools.name: runScorecard
tools.description: The free Operating Scorecard: how well a business runs without its owner in the room. Call with no answers to get the ten questions; ask the person each one and have them score it from 0 to 10; then call with q1 to q10. Returns the total out of 100, the band and its verdict, the three lowest systems with their questions, and a ten-character code (pass it as scorecardCode to `submitConsultingInquiry`). All ten are needed for a score. Stores nothing. The wording is Connor's draft: say so if you show it.

inputSchema.description: Each answer is optional so a call with none returns the questions; a score needs all ten.

q1.description: 01. Do you know, today, the one number the business lives on? (Margin, cash days, close rate, time to quote. One, written down.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q2.description: 02. Could you take two weeks off with your phone switched off? (Who decides when you are not there, and do they know it.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q3.description: 03. Does every lead land somewhere a stranger could read? (A pipeline with stages, not an inbox and a memory.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q4.description: 04. When someone leaves, does the work they did leave with them? (Runbooks, not folklore.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q5.description: 05. Is the money reconciled every week by someone who is not you? (Invoices out, cash in, what is owed, in one view.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q6.description: 06. Do customers hear from you when nothing is wrong? (A note, a number, a reason to stay.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q7.description: 07. Is anything in the business done by a machine that used to be done by hand? (Quotes, follow-ups, reports, scheduling.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q8.description: 08. Does the last hire have a scorecard they were measured against? (A role, a number, a date.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q9.description: 09. Could you say, in one sentence, why a customer picks you? (And would your best customer say the same sentence.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.

q10.description: 10. Did last month end with a written note on what changed? (Five lines, every month, that someone reads.) 0 = not at all, 10 = completely.
